title: About Display ads and the Google Display Network

facts.fact: The Google Display Network reaches people across 35 million websites and apps, plus Google-owned properties such as YouTube and Gmail, according to Google.
facts.quote: Display campaigns can reach people worldwide across 35 million websites and apps, and on Google-owned properties (YouTube and Gmail).

facts.fact: Existing Smart Display campaigns have been migrated into the unified Display campaign structure without any action needed from advertisers, and Google states this should not cause performance fluctuations.
facts.quote: Any existing Smart Display campaigns in your account will have migrated to this unified Display campaign structure without any action needed on your part.

facts.fact: Google states the migration of Smart Display campaigns into Display campaigns shouldn't cause any fluctuations in campaign performance.
facts.quote: This migration shouldn't cause any fluctuations in your campaign's performance.

facts.fact: Optimized targeting is set as the default targeting method for Display campaigns.
facts.quote: Optimized targeting is set as the default targeting method for your Display campaigns.

facts.fact: Advertisers can pay for conversions instead of clicks on Display campaigns that use Target CPA bidding, selected under the 'Pay for' header in the Bidding section.
facts.quote: You can pay for conversions, instead of clicks on Display campaigns that use Target CPA bidding.

facts.fact: Google states that advertisers can use its library of images for responsive display ads at no cost.
facts.quote: You can also use our library of images at no cost.

facts.fact: Google states that Display campaigns optimize within days.
Uploaded image Display ads can be created as images in different sizes or as HTML5.
facts.quote: You can upload ads as images in different sizes or HTML5.

facts.fact: Changes in the Display Network, such as adjustments to bids, budget, or targeting, can take 12–24 hours to apply and may not show right away.
facts.quote: Changes in the Display Network, such as adjustments to bids, budget, or targeting, can take 12–24 hours to apply and may not show right away.

facts.fact: Major structural changes, such as creating a new campaign or bid strategy, may display a temporary "Learning" status for up to 7 days.
facts.quote: Major structural changes, like creating a new campaign or bid strategy, may display a temporary "Learning" status for up to 7 days.

facts.fact: Reactivating a Google Ads campaign that has been paused for an extended period restarts the learning phase.
facts.quote: If your campaign has been paused for an extended period, reactivating it will also restart the learning phase.

facts.fact: When multiple changes are made within a 24 hour period, they may be applied outside of the chronological order of change history.
facts.quote: When there are multiple changes made within a 24 hour period, they may be applied outside of the chronological order of change history.

facts.fact: Google advises setting up a Display campaign a few days before launch and setting the start date in the future.
facts.quote: You may want to set up your campaign a few days before the launch and set the start date in the future.
